entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 5 Mi 5:1-15 . The Calamities Which Precede Messiah's Advent. His Kingdom, Conquest of Jacob's Foes, and Blessing upon His People. 1. gather thyself in troops-- that is, thou shalt do so, to resist the enemy. Lest the faithful should fall into carnal security because of the previous promises, he reminds them of the calamities which are to precede the prosperity. daughter of troops-- Jerusalem is so called on account of her numerous troops. he hath laid siege-- the enemy hath. they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek-- the greatest of insults to an Oriental. Zedekiah, the judge (or king, Am 2:3 ) of Israel, was loaded with insults by the Chaldeans; so also the other princes and judges ( La 3:30 ). Hengstenberg thinks the expression, "the judge," marks a time when no king of the house of David reigned. The smiting on the cheek of other judges of Israel was a type of the same indignity offered to Him who nevertheless is the Judge, not only of Israel, but also of the world, and who is "from everlasting" ( Mi 5:2 ; Is 50:6 ; Mt 26:67 ; 27:30 ).

Beth-lehem Ephratah--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Gen.48.7">Ge 48:7</reference>), or, Beth-lehem Judah; so called to distinguish it from Beth-lehem in Zebulun. It is a few miles southwest of Jerusalem. Beth-lehem means "the house of bread"; Ephratah means "fruitful": both names referring to the fertility of the region.<div eID="gen23684" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23685" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">though thou be little among--</hi>though thou be scarcely large enough to be reckoned among, &c. It was insignificant in size and population; so that in <reference osisRef="Josh.15.21">Jos 15:21</reference>, &c., it is not enumerated among the cities of Judah; nor in the list in <reference osisRef="Neh.11.25">Ne 11:25</reference>, &c. Under Rehoboam it became a city: <reference osisRef="2Chr.11.6">2Ch 11:6</reference>, "He built Beth-lehem." <reference osisRef="Matt.2.6">Mt 2:6</reference> seems to contradict Micah, "thou art not the least," But really he, by an independent testimony of the Spirit, confirms the prophet, Little in worldly importance, thou art not least (that is, far from least, yea, the very greatest) among the thousands, of princes of Judah, in the spiritual significance of being the birthplace of Messiah (<reference osisRef="John.7.42">Joh 7:42</reference>). God chooses the little things of the world to eclipse in glory its greatest things (<reference osisRef="Judg.6.15">Jud 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.46">Joh 1:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.27">1Co 1:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.28">28</reference>). The low state of David's line when Messiah was born is also implied here.<div eID="gen23685" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23686" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thousands--</hi>Each tribe was divided into clans or "thousands" (each thousand containing a thousand families: like our old English division of counties into hundreds), which had their several heads or "princes"; hence in <reference osisRef="Matt.2.6">Mt 2:6</reference> it is quoted "princes," substantially the same as in Micah, and authoritatively explained in Matthew. It is not so much this thousand that is preferred to the other thousands of Judah, but the Governor or Chief Prince out of it, who is preferred to the governors of all the other thousands. It is called a "town" (rather in the Greek, "village"), <reference osisRef="John.7.42">Joh 7:42</reference>; though scarcely containing a thousand inhabitants, it is ranked among the "thousands" or larger divisions of the tribe, because of its being the cradle of David's line, and of the Divine Son of David. Moses divided the people into thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, with their respective "rulers" (<reference osisRef="Exod.18.25">Ex 18:25</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="1Sam.10.19">1Sa 10:19</reference>).<div eID="gen23686" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23687" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto me--</hi>unto God the Father (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.32">Lu 1:32</reference>): to fulfil all the Father's will and purpose from eternity. So the Son declares (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.7">Psa 2:7</reference>; 40:7, 8; <reference osisRef="John.4.34">Joh 4:34</reference>); and the Father confirms it (<reference osisRef="Matt.3.17">Mt 3:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.12.18">12:18</reference>, compare with <reference osisRef="Isa.42.1">Is 42:1</reference>). God's glory is hereby made the ultimate end of redemption.<div eID="gen23687" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23688" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ruler--</hi>the "Shiloh," "Prince of peace," "on whose shoulders the government is laid" (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.10">Ge 49:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.9.6">Is 9:6</reference>). In <reference osisRef="2Sam.23.3">2Sa 23:3</reference>, "He that ruleth over men must be just," the same Hebrew word is employed; Messiah alone realizes David's ideal of a ruler. Also in <reference osisRef="Jer.30.21">Jr 30:21</reference>, "their governor shall proceed from the midst of them"; answering closely to "out of thee shall come forth the ruler," here (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.11.1-Isa.11.4">Is 11:1-4</reference>).<div eID="gen23688" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23689" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">goings forth ... from everlasting--</hi>The plain antithesis of this clause, to "come forth out of thee" (from Beth-lehem), shows that the eternal generation of the Son is meant. The terms convey the strongest assertion of infinite duration of which the Hebrew language is capable (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.90.2">Psa 90:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.8.22">Pr 8:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Prov.8.23">23</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.1.1">Joh 1:1</reference>). Messiah's generation as man coming forth unto God to do His will on earth is from Beth-lehem; but as Son of God, His goings forth are from everlasting. The promise of the Redeemer at first was vaguely general (<reference osisRef="Gen.3.15">Ge 3:15</reference>). Then the Shemitic division of mankind is declared as the quarter in which He was to be looked for (<reference osisRef="Gen.9.26">Ge 9:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.9.27">27</reference>); then it grows clearer, defining the race and nation whence the Deliverer should come, namely, the seed of Abraham, the Jews (<reference osisRef="Gen.12.3">Ge 12:3</reference>); then the particular tribe, Judah (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.10">Ge 49:10</reference>); then the family, that of David (<reference osisRef="Ps.89.19">Psa 89:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.89.20">20</reference>); then the very town of His birth, here. And as His coming drew nigh, the very parentage (<reference osisRef="Matt.1.1-Matt.1.17">Mt 1:1-17</reference>; Lu 1:26-35; 2:1-7); and then all the scattered rays of prophecy concentrate in Jesus, as their focus (<reference osisRef="Heb.1.1">He 1:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.1.2">2</reference>). <div eID="gen23689" type="x-p"/>

So the Son declares ( Psa 2:7 ; 40:7, 8; Joh 4:34 ); and the Father confirms it ( Mt 3:17 ; 12:18 , compare with Is 42:1 ). Then the Shemitic division of mankind is declared as the quarter in which He was to be looked for ( Ge 9:26 , 27 ); then it grows clearer, defining the race and nation whence the Deliverer should come, namely, the seed of Abraham, the Jews ( Ge 12:3 ); then the particular tribe, Judah ( Ge 49:10 ); then the family, that of David ( Psa 89:19 , 20 ); then the very town of His birth, here. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12770"/><div sID="gen23690" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12770"/>3. "Therefore (because of His settled plan) will God give up to their foes His people Israel, until," &c.<div eID="gen23690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23691" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">she which travaileth hath brought forth--</hi>namely, "the virgin" mother, mentioned by Micah's contemporary, <reference osisRef="Isa.7.14">Is 7:14</reference>. Zion "in travail" (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.9">Mi 4:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.10">10</reference>) answers to the virgin in travail of Messiah. Israel's deliverance from her long travail-pains of sorrow will synchronize with the appearance of the Messiah as her Redeemer (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.26">Ro 11:26</reference>) in the last days, as the Church's spiritual deliverance synchronized with the virgin's giving birth to Him at His first advent. The ancient Church's travail-like waiting for Messiah is represented by the virgin's travail. Hence, both may be meant. It cannot be restricted to the Virgin Mary: for Israel is still "given up," though Messiah has been "brought forth" eighteen and a half centuries ago. But the Church's throes are included, which are only to be ended when Christ, having been preached for a witness to all nations, shall at last appear as the Deliverer of Jacob, and when the times of the Gentiles shall be fulfilled, and Israel as a nation shall be born in a day (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.7-Isa.66.11">Is 66:7-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.21.24">Lu 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.12.1">Re 12:1</reference>, 2, 4; compare <reference osisRef="Rom.8.22">Ro 8:22</reference>).<div eID="gen23691" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23692" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">Mi 4:7</reference>). The remainder of the Israelites dispersed in foreign lands shall return to join their countrymen in Canaan. The Hebrew for "unto" is, literally, "upon," implying superaddition to those already gathered. <div eID="gen23692" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12771"/><div sID="gen23693" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12771"/><hi type="bold">4. he shall stand--</hi>that is, persevere: implying the endurance of His kingdom [Calvin]. The One just mentioned; He and He alone. Emphatical for Messiah (compare <reference osisRef="Gen.5.29">Ge 5:29</reference>).<div eID="gen23699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23700" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the peace--</hi>the fountainhead of peace between God and man, between Israel and Israel's justly offended God (<reference osisRef="Gen.49.10">Ge 49:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.9.6">Is 9:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.2.14">Ep 2:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.1.20">Col 1:20</reference>), and, as the consequence, the fountain of "peace on earth," where heretofore all is strife (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.3">Mi 4:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.18">Ho 2:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.9.10">Zec 9:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.2.14">Lu 2:14</reference>).<div eID="gen23700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23701" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the Assyrian--</hi>Being Israel's most powerful foe at that time, Assyria is made the representative of all the foes of Israel in all ages, who shall receive their final destruction at Messiah's appearing (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.1-Ezek.38.23">Eze 38:1-23</reference>).<div eID="gen23701" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23702" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seven shepherds, and eight--</hi>"Seven" expresses perfection; "seven and eight" is an idiom for a full and sufficient number (<reference osisRef="Job.5.19">Job 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Prov.6.16">Pr 6:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eccl.11.2">Ec 11:2</reference>).<div eID="gen23702" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23703" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">principal men--</hi>literally, "anointed (humble) men" (<reference osisRef="Ps.62.9">Psa 62:9</reference>), such as the apostles were. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12773"/><div sID="gen23704" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12773"/><hi type="bold">6. waste--</hi>literally, "eat up": following up the metaphor of "shepherds" (compare <reference osisRef="Num.22.4">Nu 22:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.6.3">Jr 6:3</reference>).<div eID="gen23704" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23705" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">land of Nimrod--</hi>Babylon (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.10">Mi 4:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.10.10">Ge 10:10</reference>); or, including Assyria also, to which he extended his borders (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.11">Ge 10:11</reference>).<div eID="gen23705" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23706" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the entrances--</hi>the passes into Assyria (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.3.21">2Ki 3:21</reference>). The Margin and Jerome, misled by a needless attention to the parallelism, "with the sword," translate, "with her own naked swords"; as in <reference osisRef="Ps.55.21">Psa 55:21</reference> the Hebrew is translated. But "in the entrances" of Assyria, answers to, "within our borders." As the Assyrians invade our borders, so shall their own borders or "entrances" be invaded.<div eID="gen23706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23707" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he ... he--</hi>Messiah shall deliver us, when the Assyrian shall come. <div eID="gen23707" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12774"/><div sID="gen23708" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12774"/><hi type="bold">7. remnant of Jacob--</hi>already mentioned in <reference osisRef="Mic.5.3">Mi 5:3</reference>. It in comparative smallness stands in antithesis to the "many people." Though Israel be but a remnant amidst many nations after her restoration, yet she shall exercise the same blessed influence in quickening them spiritually that the small imperceptible dew exercises in refreshing the grass (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.2">De 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.72.6">Psa 72:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.110.3">110:3</reference>). The influence of the Jews restored from Babylon in making many Gentile proselytes is an earnest of a larger similar effect hereafter (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.19">Is 66:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.8.13">Zec 8:13</reference>).<div eID="gen23708" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23709" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the Lord--</hi>Israel's restoration and the consequent conversion of the Gentiles are solely of grace.<div eID="gen23709" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23710" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tarrieth not for man--</hi>entirely God's work, as independent of human contrivance as the dew and rains that fertilize the soil. <div eID="gen23710" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12775"/><div sID="gen23711" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12775"/><hi type="bold">8. as a lion--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Mic.5.7">Mi 5:7</reference> Israel's benignant influence on the nations is described; but here her vengeance on the godless hosts who assail her (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.15">Is 66:15</reference>, 16, 19, 24; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.3">Zec 12:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.6.8">6, 8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.6.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.17">14:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.14.18">18</reference>). Judah will be "as as lion," not in respect to its cruelty, but in its power of striking terror into all opponents. Under the Maccabees, the Jews acquired Idumea, Samaria, and parts of the territory of Ammon and Moab [Grotius]. But this was only the earnest of their future glory on their coming restoration. <div eID="gen23711" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12776"/><div sID="gen23712" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12776"/><hi type="bold">9. Thine hand shall be lifted up--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Isa.26.11">Is 26:11</reference> it is Jehovah's hand that is lifted up; here Israel's as <reference osisRef="Mic.5.8">Mi 5:8</reference> implies, just as "Zion" is addressed and directed to "beat in pieces many people" (<reference osisRef="Mic.4.13">Mi 4:13</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.54.15">Is 54:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.54.17">17</reference>). For Israel's foes are Jehovah's foes. When her hand is said to be lifted up, it is Jehovah's hand that strikes the foe by her (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.13.9">Ex 13:9</reference>, with <reference osisRef="Exod.14.8">Ex 14:8</reference>). <div eID="gen23712" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12777"/><div sID="gen23713" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12777"/><hi type="bold">10. cut off thy horses ... chariots--</hi>namely, those used for the purposes of war. Israel had been forbidden the use of cavalry, or to go to Egypt for horses (<reference osisRef="Deut.17.16">De 17:16</reference>), lest they should trust in worldly forces, rather than in God (<reference osisRef="Ps.20.7">Psa 20:7</reference>). Solomon had disregarded this command (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.26">1Ki 10:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.28">28</reference>). Hereafter, saith God, I will remove these impediments to the free course of My grace: horses, chariots, &c., on which ye trust. The Church will never be safe, till she is stripped of all creature trusts, and rests on Jehovah alone [Calvin]. The universal peace given by God shall cause warlike instruments to be needless. He will cut them off from Israel (<reference osisRef="Zech.9.10">Zec 9:10</reference>); as she will cut them off from Babylon, the representative of the nations (<reference osisRef="Jer.50.37">Jr 50:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.51.21">51:21</reference>). <div eID="gen23713" type="x-p"/>
